claims.text: A W-Mo-Ta-Zr refractory high-entropy alloy can serve as a low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
W, Mo, Ta, and Zr together form a stable, disordered solid solution.
The WMoTaZr solid solution resists phase separation under extreme thermal loads.
The WMoTaZr solid solution resists phase separation under irradiation.
The selected W, Mo, Ta, and Zr elements avoid the production of long-lived radioactive isotopes.
The proposed initial material is a homogenized, polycrystalline WMoTaZr refractory HEA produced by vacuum arc melting.
Maintaining a disordered solid-solution phase supports the alloy's high-temperature strength.
Stable grain boundaries support the alloy's high-temperature strength.
Maintaining a disordered solid-solution phase supports irradiation resistance.
Stable grain boundaries support irradiation resistance.
The selected refractory elements have high melting points.
Selecting refractory elements with high melting points helps the alloy maintain mechanical integrity under thermal stress.
The robust disordered structure impedes diffusion-driven segregation and phase decomposition.
Avoiding elements that yield long-lived activation products minimizes the induction of long-lived radioactive isotopes.
After fusion-relevant exposure, the WMoTaZr HEA should retain high-temperature strength and ductility.
After fusion-relevant exposure, the WMoTaZr HEA should show limited irradiation-induced degradation.
The residual radioactivity of irradiated WMoTaZr should be lower than or comparable to that of conventional low-activation materials such as some ferritic/martensitic steels.
